To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 5′ UTR of tnpA is processed to produce an sRNA, tnpA, which regulates the expression of over 80 genes, including genes involved in SPI-1 effector protein expression.
a transposon-derived sRNA regulates gene expression in S. Typhi and S. Typhirium, and that the tnpASRN represses expression of the SPI-1 effector genes.
the IS200 transposon produces a regulatory RNA that acts as a ‘sponge’ for InvF mRNA and controls expression of SPI-1 genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how bacterial pathogens sense and respond to their environment.
how bacterial pathogens sense and respond to the host environment.
the identification of novel sRNAs and the elucidation of the mechanisms by which sRNAs regulate gene expression in Salmonellae and other bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tnpAs derived sRNA regulates the expression of over 80 genes, including the SPI-1 encoded effector proteins, by base-pairing with invF mRNA.
we have identified an sRNA derived from the IS200 transposon that regulates expression of over 80 genes in Salmonella.
the 5′ UTR of IS200 transposable element is processed to produce a regulatory RNA, which represses the expression of genes involved in invasion and growth of Salmonella typhimurium in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5' UTR of the tnpA mRNA is processed to produce an sRNA that regulates the expression of genes involved in invasion and virulence.
we identified a new class of bacterial sRNAs that are encoded in protein-coding regions and are derived from transposons, which are important regulators of bacterial virulence and metabolism.
a small RNA encoded in the 5'UTR of a transposase gene is processed from the mRNA and base-pairs to the 3'UTR of an mRNA to repress its expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5’UTR of the tnpA gene encodes a regulatory RNA that affects gene expression in Salmonellae.
the 5’ UTR of IS200 transposable element encodes a small RNA that represses expression of the invF gene.
the tnpAs derived sRNA is a key regulator of Salmonella pathogenesis.
